skill.name: tool-design
skill.description: Design agent-facing tools with clear descriptions, schemas, response formats, names, and recovery-focused errors. Use it for single tools, tool catalogs, MCP naming, and tool consolidation decisions.
skill.summary: Guides reliable agent tool design, schema clarity, MCP naming, and error recovery.
skill.author: muratcankoylan

security_audit.summary: The audit confirmed the architectural reduction guidance contains command execution examples and advice to expose shell-style primitives. Most other static matches are false positives from Markdown, docstrings, or general design prose; no prompt injection or exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: Arbitrary command execution examples may be copied into production without enough controls.
remediation.suggestion: Add explicit deny-by-default sandbox requirements, allowlists, resource limits, audit logging, and privilege boundaries beside each command execution example.

remediation.issue: Architectural reduction advice can understate security constraints for shell and filesystem access.
remediation.suggestion: Move safety constraints and non-use cases before recommending primitive command tools.

remediation.issue: Markdown examples create noisy static matches for external command patterns.
remediation.suggestion: Clarify that fenced code blocks are illustrative and are not install-time execution paths.

content.value_statement: Agent systems fail when tools have vague descriptions, overlapping purposes, or weak error messages. This skill helps teams design clear tool contracts, schemas, naming, responses, and recovery paths.
actual_capabilities: Structures tool descriptions around purpose, activation triggers, inputs, returns, and errors.
Defines naming and namespacing conventions for MCP and larger tool catalogs.
Explains when to consolidate overlapping tools into broader workflow tools.
Provides patterns for concise and detailed response formats.
Includes Python helpers for generating and evaluating tool descriptions.
Documents error message formats that support agent self-correction.
limitations: It provides guidance and helper utilities, not a complete production tool server.
Command execution examples require strict sandboxing before any production use.
Case study claims should be validated against each target system.
It does not replace security review for tools with privileged access.

use_cases.title: Audit a Tool Catalog
use_cases.description: Review existing tools for overlap, unclear activation rules, inconsistent names, and weak error recovery.

use_cases.title: Design an MCP Interface
use_cases.description: Create namespaced tool names, clear schemas, and predictable response formats for a multi-server MCP setup.

use_cases.title: Improve Agent Reliability
use_cases.description: Rewrite vague tool descriptions and error messages so agents select tools and recover from failures more accurately.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Tool Contract
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for one new tool.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a tool contract for this agent task: [task]. Include purpose, when to use it, inputs, returns, and errors.

prompt_templates.title: Review Tool Clarity
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate audit of a current tool description.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this tool description for clarity, completeness, actionability, and consistency: [description]. Suggest a revised version.

prompt_templates.title: Consolidate a Tool Set
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these tools for overlap and routing ambiguity: [tool list]. Recommend which tools to merge, split, rename, or remove.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Full MCP Catalog
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced design for a multi-server agent environment.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an MCP tool catalog for [system]. Include namespaces, naming rules, schemas, response formats, and recovery-focused errors.

output_examples.input: A team asks why its agent picks the wrong customer search tool.
output_examples.output: The skill identifies overlapping activation rules, recommends one consolidated lookup tool, and drafts clearer selection guidance.

output_examples.input: A developer needs better validation errors for a scheduling tool.
output_examples.output: The skill proposes specific error codes, expected input formats, retry guidance, and examples agents can use to self-correct.

output_examples.input: An MCP server has several generic tool names such as search and create.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends fully qualified names, domain prefixes, and consistent parameter names across related tools.

best_practices: Define purpose, activation triggers, inputs, returns, and errors before implementation.
Keep the catalog small enough that each tool has a distinct use case.
Test descriptions with representative agent requests and refine based on failures.
anti_patterns: Publishing tools with vague descriptions such as search or handle request.
Adding narrow overlapping tools when one workflow tool would reduce routing ambiguity.
Returning generic errors that do not explain what the agent should change.

faq.question: Does this skill build tools automatically?
faq.answer: No. It guides tool interface design and includes helper utilities for descriptions and schemas.

faq.question: Can it help with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance applies to agent tools used across Claude, Codex, Claude Code, and MCP environments.

faq.question: When should I use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it when designing, auditing, consolidating, naming, or documenting agent-facing tools.

faq.question: Does it cover MCP naming?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends fully qualified server and tool names to reduce collisions in multi-server setups.

faq.question: What is the main security concern?
faq.answer: Some architectural reduction examples discuss command execution tools. Those patterns require strict sandboxing and access controls.

faq.question: Does it replace evaluation?
faq.answer: No. It helps design better tools, but teams still need tests that measure agent behavior.
